--- the same five predicates against the controls (main-debug) ---
A '!' marks a predicate firing on an input that is NOT the defect.

                      P1      P2      P3      P4      P5       exit       what it is
control-static        .       .       .       .       .        0x00000000  the object made `static`, so mutable: compiles, exit 0
control-memberfn      .       .       .       .       .        0x00000000  member function on a mutable local: compiles, exit 0
control-constlocal    .       .       .       .       .        0x00000000  const *local* object, same violation: compiles, exit 0
control-syntaxerr     .       .       .       .       !        0x80004005  ordinary syntax error: E_FAIL, SAME status as the repro

--- why they differ ---
Four faces and two silences, all of the same defect. The stack is identical
where it can be read (manual-case-cast-stack.txt): a store to a $Globals-backed
object reaches TranslateCBAddressUserLegacy's `// Must be GEP here`.

P2 is the measured counterfactual the brief warned about. E_FAIL is
deliberately NOT in triage.py's INTERNAL_STATUS, because an ordinary syntax
error exits with it too -- see the control-syntaxerr row, which has the SAME
exit status as the repro. So exit status alone reports this still-open 2022
issue as fixed at v1.7.2207 (2022-07), four years early and wrong today.

P3 and P4 fail in the other direction: they invent a regression at a release
where only the *wording* changed. Two releases print nothing at all.

P5 gets the release history right here, and is still the wrong predicate: it
fires on the syntax-error control, so on any other issue it would invent a
crash from a clean diagnosed failure. Being accidentally right on one issue
is not the same as being right.

Both halves of is_internal_failure() are load-bearing: the status codes carry
v1.4.1907..v1.6.2112, and the build-agnostic 'cast<...>() argument' marker
carries v1.7.2207..main. Neither alone recovers the true range.
